exposure: causes for preferred mode of delivery (e.g., faster recovery, easy baby bonding, fear from cesarean section, short hospital stay, avoiding labor pain, fear on baby's life, lack of knowledge, fear from vaginal delivery)
cohort: 150 Iraqi primiparous women who attended the gynecology clinic in Baghdad teaching hospital/medical city.
finding: The majority of Iraqi primiparous women (68.7%) expressed a preference for vaginal delivery, while 31.3% preferred cesarean section, driven by various factors.
mod_finding: The study identified that 68.7% of primiparous women preferred vaginal delivery citing faster recovery and easy baby bonding, whereas 31.3% preferred cesarean section to avoid labor pain and due to fear for the baby's life.
